title: Coverage and whole containers
hook: A label says 8m² per litre. Fractional need is not a whole-container order.

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Distinguish continuous material need from indivisible container purchases.

misconception: A fractional material requirement can always be purchased exactly.
objective: Distinguish continuous material need from indivisible container purchases.

claims.text: A fictional coverage label states 8m² per litre. Containers hold 1L; coverage is assumed exact. Scaled model; hypothetical coverage; no application guidance.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Area=10m², A=2L and B=1.25L. Geometry follows the declared dimension relationships. Other pictures use a fixed full scale across the slider range; continuous fills and arcs show relative amounts rather than literal object counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["ceil",["/","x",8]]; B=["/","x",8]; x denotes Area. At x=10, A=2, B=1.25. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. Diagram scale: resourceGraphicScale in resource-model.ts takes the maximum modeled magnitude across both formulas and the declared slider range. For non-geometry figures, full-scale values are displayed; the scale stays fixed when the slider changes. Energy axis endpoints use resourceAxisEnd, including B=5×A hours in lh-watts-hours-trade; cylinder rx and ry both scale with radius in resourceCylinderDimensions. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: Area divided by coverage gives modeled exact volume. The whole-container order rounds that result up. This ignores surface losses and product variation, so it teaches order arithmetic rather than actual application instructions.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["ceil",["/","x",8]]; B=["/","x",8]; x denotes Area. At x=10, A=2, B=1.25. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. The principle follows from those expressions and stated scenario limits. claims.text: A fictional label states 8m² per litre; containers hold 1L and cannot be split. How many containers for 17m²? Correct: 3. 17 ÷ 8 = 2.125L exactly, and whole containers round that up to 3.
